nodes.summary: The germ σ-algebra is contained in every positive-time component of the filtration.
nodes.title: Germ sigma-algebra lies in every positive-time level

nodes.summary: The *germ σ-algebra at `0`* of a filtration `𝓕` indexed by `NNReal`, defined as the intersection `⨅_{t > 0} 𝓕_t`. For Brownian motion this is the `𝓕_0^+` σ-algebra of events observable "immediately after" time `0`. Ported verbatim from `v1/Atlas/TheoryOfProbability/code/Blumenthal01.lean`.
nodes.title: Germ sigma-algebra at time zero

nodes.summary: A continuous process `B : NNReal → Ω → E` with independent increments, started at `x` and adapted to `𝓕`. The measure is a probability measure, `B 0 = x` a.e., each increment after `s` is independent of `𝓕 s`, and a.e. paths are continuous. These are the five meaningful fields of the archived v1 specification; its tautological pushforward-law field is omitted. No Gaussian-law or stationary-increment condition is…
nodes.title: Continuous process with independent increments

nodes.summary: Each `B u` is measurable with respect to the natural filtration at any later time `t`.
nodes.title: Process is measurable for its natural filtration at later times

nodes.summary: Each coordinate of the adapted continuous process is measurable.
nodes.title: Coordinates of a continuous independent-increment process are measurable

nodes.summary: The natural filtration is contained in any filtration to which `B` is adapted.
nodes.title: Natural filtration is the smallest adapted filtration

nodes.summary: The natural filtration of a process: `𝓕^nat_t = σ(B_u : u ≤ t)`. Unlike Mathlib's `Filtration.natural`, this is built from measurability rather than strong measurability, which is all that is available from adaptedness.
nodes.title: Natural filtration of a process

nodes.summary: The germ σ-algebra of the natural filtration of `B`.
nodes.title: Germ sigma-algebra of the natural filtration

nodes.summary: Every event in the natural germ of a continuous process with independent increments and a deterministic a.e. initial value has probability `0` or `1`. This general form includes the classical Brownian natural-filtration law.
nodes.title: Blumenthal zero-one law
